topic: Returning to running after a break

slides.headline: Back to running after months off?
slides.sub: A gradual plan that respects what your body can handle right now.

slides.title: Start lower than you think
slides.body: Your heart and lungs often bounce back faster than your tendons and bones. A good starting point is walk-run intervals, like one minute jogging and two minutes walking, for 20 to 30 minutes.

slides.title: Build one thing at a time
slides.body: Increase time before pace. Add a little each week and run every second day at first. Every third or fourth week, hold steady or ease back slightly to let your body catch up.

slides.title: Use the next-morning test
slides.body: Mild soreness during a run that settles by the next morning is usually fine. Pain that's worse the next day, or changes how you run, means easing back to the previous step.

slides.title: Add strength twice a week
slides.body: Calf raises, split squats, bridges and step-ups build capacity for running. Two short sessions a week, around 20 minutes each, is a good starting point for most people.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Pain in one spot on a bone, pain that's worse each run, swelling, a limp or pain at night should be assessed before you keep building. Getting it checked early usually keeps the plan simpler.

slides.headline: Want a return-to-run plan?
slides.body: Our Sydney CBD and Chatswood physios look at your strength and running history, then map out a gradual plan you can follow week by week.

caption:
Dusting off the runners after a long break? Your lungs might be keener than your legs.

Fitness often comes back faster than tendons and bones adapt, which is why a gradual return pays off. Start with walk-run intervals, increase time before pace, and run every second day at first. Every few weeks, hold steady to let your body catch up.

Use the next-morning test: mild soreness that settles overnight is usually fine, but pain that's worse the next day means easing back a step. Add calf raises, split squats and bridges twice a week. Pain in one spot on a bone, a limp or pain at night should be checked before you keep building.
